title: Runtime choice storyboard — SE pocket deck (draft)
abstract: A concise, SE-focused storyboard to run 10–15 minute pilot qualification calls where runtime/model choices, quantization tradeoffs, and fallback economics matter. Purpose: give sellers an action-oriented narrative, three canonical customer profiles, and 6 quick scripts to win buy-in and shape a follow-up pilot scope.
goal: Enable an SE to convert a discovery call into a scoped pilot and an initial capacity recommendation by focusing the conversation on real runtime tradeoffs and mitigations that matter to engineering stakeholders.
slide_outline: 1 — Opener: one-sentence positioning (why runtime choices matter for your use case)
2 — Agenda + expected outcome (pilot scope, success metrics, next 3 actions)
4 — Quick diagnostic checklist (Qs to ask: p95, qps, payload size, cacheability, PII)
5 — Runtime-choice decision map (hosted -> dedicated -> private) — TL;DR guidance
6 — Quantization & quality tradeoffs (concrete example: 8-bit vs 4-bit impact on latency/TFLOPs)
7 — Fallback plan patterns (model variant fallthroughs, regional routing, burst capacity)
8 — Economic shorthand (ballpark per-1M tokens across options + caching uplift examples)
9 — Pilot template (3-week technical pilot with metrics to capture: p50/p95, throughput, error modes)
10 — Common objections & scripts (3x rapid rebuttals with evidence hooks)
11 — Can we run this with you? (explicit ask + next-steps checklist)
speaker_notes: Slide 1: Frame the question with a one-line problem statement: customers pick the wrong runtime because they optimize for headline throughput not tail-latency or unit cost.
Slide 3: Use concrete short stories: fintech checkout flow (latency-first), search/semantic retrieval (cost-sensitive), healthcare analytics (data residency). Keep each to two bullets.
Slide 4: Diagnostic: ask about request burst patterns (cron vs user-driven), average prompt length, cache hit rate expectations. Note: if cacheable > 60% the economics change drastically.
Slide 6: Give a short example: 4-bit quantization reduces GPU memory by ~2–3x and often cuts runtime cost by 30–60%; caveat: may introduce hallucination risk — mention eval set to measure.

Slide 7: Fallback pattern example: prefer cheaper quantized variant for bulk, route 5–10% of sensitive/failed requests to higher-precision hosted model; show detection heuristics (low logprob, low confidence).
Slide 8: Provide back-of-envelope math for a demo customer: 1k qps, 10 tokens avg -> tokens/day = 864M. Show cost delta hosted vs dedicated vs private with caching assumptions.
Slide 10: Objection script: 'We can't tolerate accuracy loss' — reply: 'Let's gate quantized variant behind an eval set and split traffic 95/5 to measure user-facing quality.'
Speaker tip: keep language simple, avoid heavy infra jargon unless the buyer shows appetite — the deck is a tool to surface engineers who can deep dive later.
canonical_customer_profiles: Latency-first: interactive UIs, strict p95 < 200ms requirement; willing to pay premium for low tail latency; likely to prefer Dedicated with pinned low-latency model variants.
Cost-constrained: high-volume batch or async workloads; p50 ok, but unit cost matters; good candidate for aggressive quantization + caching on Hosted or Dedicated with autoscale.
Regulated-data: needs VPC/on-prem or Private control plane; data residency and key management are top priorities; emphasis on audit logs and isolation; unit economics secondary.
pilot_template: Duration: 3 weeks (tech proof) — Week 0: config + baseline metrics; Week 1: quantized variant + cache; Week 2: stress test + fallback routing; Deliverable: p50/p95, cost per 1M tokens, failover audit log.
Success criteria (example): p95 under X ms, <Y% regression in accuracy on eval prompts, cost per 1M tokens reduced by 30% vs baseline.
Minimum artifacts needed: sample prompt set (50–200), traffic profile, SLO targets, contact for infra access (if Private).
common_objections_and_scripts: Accuracy concerns: 'We can't accept quality drop' => Script: propose evaluation on a labeled prompt set and staged rollout with user-visible gates.
Security/data concerns: 'Our data can't leave VPC' => Script: map to Private deployment checklist, note timeline and support options.
Cost skepticism: 'Numbers look optimistic' => Script: commit to a small pilot measuring real token distribution and report real cost delta, share caching uplift assumptions.
